text: Look, I am sending my messenger, and he will clear the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord whom you are seeking will come to his temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire—look, he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.

versions.text: Look, I am sending my messenger, and he will clear the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord whom you are seeking will come to his temple—the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight. Look, he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew joins "the messenger of the covenant" with a conjunction (וּמַלְאַךְ) rather than as an appositional restatement; keeping the connective preserves the sentence structure and the emphatic "look, he is coming!" that follows directly.

text: But who can endure the day of his coming? Who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire, like a launderer's soap.
He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver; he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, so that they may bring offerings to the LORD in righteousness.
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD, as in the days of old, as in years long past.

I will come near to you for judgment. I will be a swift witness against sorcerers and adulterers, against those who swear falsely, against those who defraud the hired worker of his wages, who oppress the widow and the orphan, who push aside the foreigner and do not fear me, says the LORD of hosts.
For I, the LORD, do not change; therefore you, children of Jacob, are not consumed.
Ever since the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts. But you ask, "How are we to return?"
Can a man rob God? Yet you are robbing me. But you ask, "How have we robbed you?" In the tithes and the offerings.
You are under a curse—the whole nation of you—because you are robbing me.

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in my house. Test me in this, says the LORD of hosts, and see if I will not open the windows of heaven for you and pour out on you a blessing beyond measure.
I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that it will not destroy the fruit of your soil, and the vine in your field will not fail to bear, says the LORD of hosts.
Then all the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight, says the LORD of hosts.
Your words against me have been harsh, says the LORD. Yet you ask, "What have we said against you?"
You have said, "It is pointless to serve God. What do we gain by keeping his charge and walking about in mourning before the LORD of hosts?
"So now we call the arrogant blessed. Those who do evil prosper; they put God to the test and get away with it."

versions.text: So now we call the arrogant blessed. Those who do evil prosper; they put God to the test and get away with it."
versions.explanation: The quotation opened in verse 14 is closed at the end of verse 15, but verse 15 lacks an opening quotation mark. For a continued quotation across verses, the opening mark should be repeated so readers (and oral readers) can track the speech.

text: Then those who feared the LORD spoke with one another, and the LORD listened and heard. A scroll of remembrance was written before him about those who fear the LORD and treasure his name.
They will be mine, says the LORD of hosts, my treasured possession on the day when I act. I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him.
Then once again you will see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve him.

For look, the day is coming, burning like a furnace. All the arrogant and every evildoer will be stubble, and the day that is coming will set them ablaze, says the LORD of hosts, leaving them neither root nor branch.
But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings, and you will go out leaping like calves released from the stall.
You will trample the wicked; they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day when I act, says the LORD of hosts.
Remember the law of my servant Moses, the statutes and judgments I gave him at Horeb for all Israel.
Look, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the LORD comes.
He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers; otherwise I will come and strike the land with utter destruction.

versions.text: He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers, so that I will not come and strike the land with utter destruction.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew פֶּן ("lest / otherwise") carries a warning of threatened judgment, not a purpose clause. "So that I will not come" softens the force; "otherwise I will come" preserves the warning and reads more forcefully aloud.
